title: The ad I can’t forget

fn.en: Talk about advertising; report what people said.

gr: reported speech, and the tense shift that goes with it

sub.en: When you report what somebody said, everything steps back one.

items.q: “The advert is really amusing.” → She said the advert ___ really amusing.
items.why: Present simple steps back to past simple.

items.q: “I saw an amazing ad.” → He said he ___ an amazing ad.
items.why: Past simple steps back to past perfect.

items.q: “A new law has been passed.” → The instructor told them a new law ___.
“I will never forget it.” → She said she ___ never forget it.
“Turn the light off.” → He asked his friend ___ the light off.
items.why: An instruction is reported with ask / tell + object + to + infinitive.

items.q: Which verb is followed directly by an object?
items.why: tell + person. say and explain do not take a person directly: say to me, explain to me.

items.q: “It was my fault.” → He ___ that it had been his fault.
“I should have checked it.” → She said she ___ it.
items.why: RECYCLED from Lesson 32: should have does not step back any further — it is already in the past.

acts.title: Direct → reported, in four moves
steps: She said: “I saw an amazing ad yesterday.”
She said that she had seen …
2 · Step the TENSE back: saw → had seen.
She said that she had seen an amazing ad …
3 · Keep the rest of the sentence as it is.
She said that she had seen an amazing ad the day before.
4 · Change the TIME WORD: yesterday → the day before.

tts: The best ad I’ve seen had a serious point, but it was actually really amusing. There were three men sitting outside somewhere in Australia, with a house behind them and the light on.
One of them asked another one to go and turn the light off, because it was Earth Hour — the hour when everyone is supposed to turn off their lights to save energy.
The man couldn’t be bothered. He said it was just one light and it wouldn’t make any difference.
Then, suddenly, he saw a huge cloud of moths coming towards them. Maybe every moth in Australia was heading for their light, because all the others had been switched off.
I really think the most effective adverts are the ones that make people laugh.

items.q: What is Earth Hour?
o: An hour when people turn off their lights to save energy

items.q: What did the man say when he was asked to turn the light off?
o: That it was only one light and would make no difference
That he would do it later

items.q: Why did the moths come to that house?
o: Because every other light had been switched off

tts: I saw an amazing ad to raise awareness of the problems homeless people have. It said that the weather was one of the biggest problems, and that during the previous winter many of them had died.
However, because they were homeless, nobody really noticed them.
So in Germany, Switzerland, Russia and a few other countries, they asked homeless people to present the weather forecast on television.
This helped people watching to see them as real people, and lots of them were offered help and jobs.

I also liked a public service ad called “The impossible texting and driving test”. The instructor told the learners that a new law had been passed, and that they now had to prove they could use a mobile phone while driving. Of course, nobody could do it.

items.s: The second advert was about homeless people.
Homeless people were asked to present the weather forecast.
Nobody was offered any help as a result.
The instructor told the learners a new law had been passed.
Several of the learners managed to text and drive successfully.

write.q: Write about an advertisement you cannot forget, and report what other people have said about it. Use said, told, explained, admitted and mentioned at least once each, with the correct tense shift.
plan: which advert, and what happens in it
what somebody else said about it
write.model:
The advert I can’t forget was for a road-safety campaign, and it ran for about three weeks in 2019. A driving instructor told a group of learners that a new law had been passed and that they now had to prove they could text while driving. Every one of them failed, on camera, and none of them had realized that the law did not exist.

When I showed it to my brother, he said it was manipulative. He mentioned that the learners had not agreed to be filmed for that purpose, which is a fair point. Later, though, he admitted that he had stopped answering messages at the wheel, and he explained that it was because he kept seeing the face of the third learner. I told him that was the whole point.

speak.q: Describe an advert you remember out loud, and report what two other people said about it. Watch the tense shift as you speak.
speak.model: The one I can’t forget was a road-safety advert. An instructor told the learners a new law had been passed and that they had to prove they could text while driving. Every one of them failed. My brother said it was manipulative — he mentioned that they hadn’t agreed to be filmed. But later he admitted he’d stopped answering messages at the wheel.
